whatIs.title: 1. What is WinStack
whatIs.description: WinStack is a simple, accessible web store that uses the official WinGet (Windows Package Manager) catalog to install applications on Windows 10 and 11.
whatIs.point1: Pick apps visually without memorizing package names.
whatIs.point2: We generate a native WinStack installer (.cmd) that opens a clean progress window and installs everything automatically — no PowerShell setup required.
whatIs.point3: Free, bilingual (PT/EN), and designed for quick setups.

downloadRun.title: 2. How to download and run the installer
downloadRun.intro: After building your stack in the store, follow these steps to deploy your apps:
downloadRun.step1: Open the sidebar stack and confirm all desired apps are listed.
downloadRun.step2: Click download installer to save winstack-install.cmd to your computer.
downloadRun.step3: Open your Downloads folder and double-click winstack-install.cmd.
downloadRun.step4: If Windows asks for administrator permission (UAC), click Yes — required to install software.
downloadRun.step5: Wait for the WinStack installer terminal window to open and install everything automatically.

motw.title: 3. PowerShell execution policy (does not apply to .cmd)
motw.intro: The .cmd installer bypasses PowerShell execution policy automatically. If you copy the .ps1 script manually (Advanced mode), you may see "script is not digitally signed".
motw.step1: Always prefer the winstack-install.cmd file from the site — just double-click it.
motw.step2: The .cmd requests administrator permission when needed and runs PowerShell with execution policy bypass.
motw.step3: If you still run the .ps1 directly, open PowerShell and run: powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\winstack-install.ps1
motw.step5: For scripts downloaded from the internet, Windows may also apply Mark-of-the-Web — see below.
motw.tip: Tip: the .cmd installer automatically unblocks (MOTW) the embedded script.

installWinget.title: 4. How to install WinGet (App Installer)
installWinget.description: WinGet ships with Microsoft's App Installer. If the winget command does not work in PowerShell, install or update App Installer:
installWinget.step1: Open the Microsoft Store using the link below or search for App Installer.
installWinget.step2: Click Get or Update and wait for the installation to finish.
installWinget.storeLinkLabel: Open App Installer in Microsoft Store
installWinget.note: After installing, close and reopen PowerShell. Type winget --version to confirm it is working.

notepad.title: 5. Alternative: copy script to Notepad
notepad.intro: If Windows blocks the downloaded file, you can create the script manually and avoid Mark-of-the-Web:
notepad.step1: In the sidebar list, use the Copy script button to copy the content.
notepad.step2: Open Notepad from the Start menu.
notepad.step4: Go to File → Save As, pick a folder, and save as InstallApps.ps1 (type: All files).
notepad.step5: Run the saved file in PowerShell as administrator — no unblock step needed.

faq.title: 6. Frequently asked questions
faq.q1: Do I need to be a computer administrator?
faq.a1: In most cases, yes. The installer automatically requests administrator permission (UAC prompt) when you are not already elevated.
faq.a2: The script only installs packages you chose in the store, using Microsoft's official winget command. You can review the content in Advanced mode before downloading.
faq.a3: Yes, as long as WinGet (App Installer) is installed and up to date. Windows 11 includes WinGet by default; on Windows 10 you may need to install it from the Microsoft Store.
faq.q4: What if an app fails to install?
faq.a4: The script continues installing the remaining apps. Check your internet connection, whether the app is available in your region, and disk space. You can try installing the app individually later with winget install PackageName.
